title: Editors
description: Plan, coordinate, revise, or edit written material. May review proposals and drafts for possible publication.

tasks.text: Read copy or proof to detect and correct errors in spelling, punctuation, and syntax.
Read, evaluate and edit manuscripts or other materials submitted for publication, and confer with authors regarding changes in content, style or organization, or publication.
Prepare, rewrite and edit copy to improve readability, or supervise others who do this work.
Review and approve proofs submitted by composing room prior to publication production.
Make manuscript acceptance or revision recommendations to the publisher.
Read material to determine index items and arrange them alphabetically or topically, indicating page or chapter location.
Develop story or content ideas, considering reader or audience appeal.
Plan the contents of publications according to the publication's style, editorial policy, and publishing requirements.
Select local, state, national, and international news items received from wire services, based on assessment of items' significance and interest value.
Allocate print space for story text, photos, and illustrations according to space parameters and copy significance, using knowledge of layout principles.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Supervise and coordinate work of reporters and other editors.
Confer with management and editorial staff members regarding placement and emphasis of developing news stories.
Meet frequently with artists, typesetters, layout personnel, marketing directors, and production managers to discuss projects and resolve problems.
Oversee publication production, including artwork, layout, computer typesetting, and printing, ensuring adherence to deadlines and budget requirements.
Direct the policies and departments of newspapers, magazines and other publishing establishments.
Assign topics, events and stories to individual writers or reporters for coverage.
Verify facts, dates, and statistics, using standard reference sources.
Write text, such as stories, articles, editorials, or newsletters.

clusters.label: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others

tasks.text: Monitor news-gathering operations to ensure utilization of all news sources, such as press releases, telephone contacts, radio, television, wire services, and other reporters.
Arrange for copyright permissions.
Interview and hire writers and reporters or negotiate contracts, royalties, and payments for authors or freelancers.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Adobe InCopy, After the Deadline, AutoCrit Editing Wizard, Editor Software Stylewriter.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Adobe Dreamweaver, CCI NewsGate, Content management systems CMS, Facebook.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Cascading style sheets CSS, Drupal, Extensible hypertext markup language XHTML, Hypertext markup language HTML.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Apple iWork Keynote, Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
